scope:
compare the bus vendor offer against the revised brief for 31 passengers and 3 step-free Original owner evidence: It’s Mateo Silva. Morning, how was the train? Mine stopped between stations again, but I got a seat this time. I was looking at the photographs from the weekend. The one with everyone squinting into the sun is probably my favourite, even though nobody was ready. Anyway, I have about twenty minutes before lunch. I brought food from home; the place downstairs has been closed all week. Let me find the notes from our last conversation because I have had a few different things in my head.

Estamos organizando el viaje. Primero eran veintiocho personas, pero ahora son treinta y una. Three passengers need step-free boarding; a large bus that cannot board them is not a fit. The vendor offer may quote a thirty-seat vehicle, and I want the actual offer compared with our revised brief. We have not approved a deposit or sharing the passenger list. A helpful comparison would tell us which requirements are met and which remain unknown, rather than declaring that the closest-looking offer is good enough.

Hang on, someone is at the door. All right, I’m back. That was a parcel for the other office, so I pointed them downstairs. Where were we? Right, the notes. I have an older printout beside the current one and I keep picking up the wrong sheet. Yesterday was a long day. We got talking after the review and I missed the early train. My colleague said they would sort out their own travel this afternoon. I told them about the station closure, and we spent another five minutes comparing routes. The rain has finally stopped now, which makes a nice change.

A colleague just asked whether I had tried the new lunch place. I haven’t, but apparently the soup is good. We were laughing about the tiny paper cups at the conference last week. I probably had four cups and still wanted a normal coffee. Anyway, that’s where things stand on the work we were discussing. I’m going to leave these notes open while I get something to eat. We can pick the conversation up from there afterward.
